judged_text: The Google refresh path persists the entire zod safeParse wrapper — `{success, data}` — as `credential.key`, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the raw safeParse result while the code it replaces stored the flat output of `googleCredentialSchema.parse()`. On each user's first token refresh after deploy (Google access tokens expire hourly), the credential row is overwritten with `{"success":true,"data":{...}}`; the next GoogleCalendarService construction reads `credential.key` expecting the flat shape and gets undefined access_token/refresh_token, permanently bricking every Google Calendar integration until each user manually reconnects — the previous key is destroyed with no backup.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the *entire* Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, ... }`), not the parsed `data` payload. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow was changed from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (which returns the flat credential object) to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `key` directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This will store the safeParse wrapper shape into `credential.key`, which is incompatible with code expecting the flat credential fields (e.g., `access_token`, `refresh_token`, etc.). The finding’s core claim (persisting `{success,data}` instead of the flat parsed object) is directly verifiable from the diff.
